chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz that he said:

We intended to go out, so we came to greet Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said, 'It is as though you sought the blessing of Monday.' We said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So what day is greater in ominousness than Monday? On it we lost our Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and revelation was raised from us. Do not go out on Monday, and go out on Tuesday.'

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَاءِ: Tuesday, the day recommended for departure
key_terms.الْإِثْنَيْنِ: Monday, the day discussed as unsuitable for departure
key_terms.بَرَكَةَ: blessing or auspicious benefit sought in undertaking an act
key_terms.شُؤْمًا: ominousness or ill fortune in this context
key_terms.نَبِيَّنَا: our Prophet, referring to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام discourage travel on Monday and recommend Tuesday instead?
ai.summary: This hadith reports guidance from Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام concerning the disliked nature of beginning travel on Monday. The Imam عليه السلام links this to the historical loss of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the cessation of revelation, and recommends departing on Tuesday instead.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2400 - It is narrated from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz that he said:

"We intended to leave, so we went to bid farewell to Abu Abdullah (as).
Imam (as) said: 'It seems you are seeking the blessing of Monday.'
We said: 'Yes.'
Imam (as) said: 'What day is more ominous than Monday? On that day, we lost our Prophet (sw), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and revelation ceased to descend upon us. Do not depart on Monday; instead, depart on Tuesday.'"
